promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 3 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: You have not lost your fitness in two weeks off, so step back in close to where you left off. Let's be honest about Nov 15: finishing the 5K is realistic, running every step is a stretch.

flags.detail: all three planned walk-run sessions were missed while you were back and forth with Mum, so this week is a careful restart, not a reset to zero.

flags.detail: at 3 weeks out, running the full 5K without walking is ambitious given your longest run is 2.78 km, so I would soften the target to finishing strong.

flags.title: Longest run so far

answers.question: I haven't run for two weeks. Do I have to start again from the beginning? And is the 5K in four weeks still realistic?
answers.answer:
No, you do not start from the beginning. Two weeks off is a pause, not a wipe. Pick up one notch below where you left off and you will catch back up inside a week.

On the race, two things to be clear about. First, the race is 3 weeks away now, not 4, since it is Sun Nov 15. Second, finishing the 5K on your feet is a realistic goal from here; running every single step without walking is a stretch given the longest you have run so far is 2.78 km. I would reframe the target to "finish feeling strong, running as much of it as I can," and treat any extra as a bonus. If the next two weeks go well we can push the running portion right up to race day.

new.analysis:
The job this week is to get back on the rhythm you had in late September without overreaching. You were doing 8 x 2 min run and 1 min walk before the break, so I have you start a touch below that on Monday, repeat near your old session on Wednesday, and lengthen the run portion on Saturday. Growing the run interval matters more than adding minutes right now, because the race asks for continuous running.

Keep every run easy. If you can hold a short sentence while running, the effort is right; if you cannot, slow down. Do not try to make up for the missed weeks by going faster or longer than what is written.

Life context matters here. Six hours of sleep and high stress is not a base for hard sessions, so there is no quality work this week even though we are close to the race. Rest days are real rest, and the dog walk still counts as useful easy movement. If anything feels off, swap a run for a walk and tell me.

Next week I want to push the run intervals toward 4 to 5 minutes and include one longer effort that gets you close to 30 minutes of mostly running. That sets up a short taper into race day.

safetyCallouts.title: Look after yourself first.
safetyCallouts.body: With Mum just home and sleep at 6 hrs, if a run feels heavy swap it for a walk and tell me, and if anything hurts beyond normal tiredness please see a GP or physio before pushing on.
